title: Three Days and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：meal　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 meal 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the cook ① cooked the meal that no guest in the inn would have recorded, and he said the cooking was the whole of the day. The ② meal, meaning the dish itself and not the tray, ran three days and stayed unrecorded in the book; a meal, he said, is the only thing in an inn that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ meal in that inn had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ meal at the far stove, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A meal, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the cook said the recording is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the meal was the whole of the matter, meaning the bread and not the dish. The ⑥ meal, meaning the bread and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; meal, he said, is either something you cook or the only word that means both a dish and a bread. He said the bread is the part they remember.

By 1976 the ⑦ meal had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ meal of the whole thing, the cook wrote in October, was one inn and three days of recording; meal, he said, is either the portion at the far stove or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ meal I remember is the dish recorded in the menu, which closed in 1978 and is still recorded as the quietest in the inn. A ⑩ meal, my mother said in 1980, is the only dish that improves by being recorded; every meal, she said, is a bread that has agreed to look like a dish. She said the bread was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 一餐；一顿饭（指小馆里每一顿旁边的那一顿）
B. n. 一餐；一顿饭（指那顿一顿饭本身，与托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：cook the meal 做这一顿饭
D. n. 一餐；一顿饭（指留给孩子们分的那一盘那一顿）
E. n. 开饭之事（抽象总称，指一处小馆的一顿饭之事）
F. n. 一餐；一顿饭（指菜单里写到、被记载的的那一顿）
G. n. 饭食、生计（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 生计（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cooked the meal that no guest in the inn would have recorded
The meal, meaning the dish itself and not the tray
the meal at the far stove
the meal was the whole of the matter
the meal had become a line in a menu
The meal of the whole thing
A meal, my mother said in 1980

answers.why: cook the meal 意为“做这一顿饭”，1971 年那位厨子把小馆里没有一位客人肯记载的一顿饭做了一遍。
meal 意为“一餐；一顿饭”，指那顿一顿饭本身而不是托盘，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被记载。
meal 意为“一餐；一顿饭”，指小馆里每一顿旁边的那一顿，每一顿旁边都有同一只小小的托盘。
meal 意为“一餐；一顿饭”，指最远那座炉边留给孩子们分的那一盘那一顿，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
meal 意为“饭食、生计”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份饭食就是那件事的全部。
meal 意为“生计”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那顿一顿饭，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
meal 意为“一餐；一顿饭”，指菜单里写到、被记载的的那一顿，到 1976 年这一顿成了菜单里的一行。
meal 意为“开饭之事”，厨子十月写道，整件事的一顿饭之事是一处小馆和三个日子的记载。
meal 意为“一餐；一顿饭”，我记得的是菜单里记载过的那一顿，1978 年开完了，至今仍被说成小馆里最安静的一顿。
meal 为抽象总称，母亲 1980 年说，一顿饭是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的一顿饭。
